text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT p99 streaming latency breach in shared-gpu-pool-3 — p99=6.8s (SLO 3s). Paging @ryan-oncall. Detected spike in host-level IO and KV cache evictions.

ryan-oncall: acked. I'm looking. Any more context? Which tenants are hot?

lina-sre: I'm seeing sustained cgroup writeback and IO wait on gpunode-34. KV cache evictions spiked from 2/min -> 150/min starting 00:12UTC.
logs:
```
[00:12:10] gpunode-34 io.wait=78%  cgroup.io.writeback=230MB/s  kv_evictions=152
[00:13:05] tenant=ml-batch-7 gpu_mem=94% io_ops=3200/s
```

alex-engops: `pss top` shows tenant ml-batch-7 thrashing disk and holding large GPU kernels. Likely noisy neighbor. Also seeing many streaming sessions pinned to shared-gpu-pool-3.

jess-support: we've got 3 customer tickets in the last 10m (Acme Corp, Finlytics). Reports: streaming stalls, partial frames, reconnect loops. Traces: trace-id=7854a2b9

ryan-oncall: mitigation options:
- throttle ml-batch-7 IO via cgroup blkio weight
- evict/evacuate tenant to spare hosts
- temporarily route streaming traffic off shared-gpu-pool-3 -> dedicated fallback pool
Plan: start with soft throttle then evacuation if it doesn't help. I'll run the throttle now.

lina-sre: running eviction daemon to migrate non-critical sessions. Starting drain on gpunode-34 -> gpunode-38. Estimated ~4m.
Commands I'm running:
```
# set blkio weight (soft throttle)
echo 200 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenant-ml-batch-7/blkio.weight
# trigger evictor
kubectl -n infra exec -it evictor-3 -- /usr/local/bin/evict --node gpunode-34 --target gpunode-38
```

incident-bot: Routing change applied: streaming route shared-gpu-pool-3 -> dedicated-fallback-pool (ratio 10% -> 50%). Rollout id=roll-2026-05-03-01

alex-engops: as a precaution lowering model size for streaming fallback route to small-quant model (reduces KV footprint). Will monitor quality metrics.

jess-support: customer updates queued: sending to Acme + Finlytics with ETA and mitigation steps. Noting degraded frames and reconnects.

lina-sre: throttle applied, initial metrics:
- p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 0.9s
- p99 currently 4.9s (was 6.8s)
- kv_evictions down to ~40/min
I'll continue the evacuation. If p99 stays >4s we'll evict ml-batch-7 fully.

ryan-oncall: good. I'll keep watching dashboards. @sam-oncall-2 if I need to hand off in 15m I'll pass postmortem ownership.

sam-oncall-2: standing by.

maria-cs: noted impacted customers and Sent N1 to SLA team — they asked for root cause once we stabilize.

lina-sre: evacuation complete on gpunode-34 -> gpunode-38. ml-batch-7 moved. Post-evac metrics:
- p99=2.6s (under SLO)
- streaming errors dropped to baseline

ryan-oncall: thanks everyone. Handoff: handing incident to @sam-oncall-2 for watch and postmortem. Sam, owner for follow-up actions: increase eviction sensitivity for shared pools, add IO throttling runbook, and verify autoscale thresholds on routing.

sam-oncall-2: ack. I'll own the postmortem. Initial notes: noisy-tenant detection delayed by KV eviction alarm thresholds. Actionables:
- tune kv-eviction and io.wait alerts (lower thresholds)
- add automated soft-throttle playbook
- consider tenant isolation policy for high-throughput batch jobs

incident-bot: Incident auto-closed for paging oncall (notifications muted) — reopen if p99 >3s in next 30m.

ryan-oncall: adding a quick blameless triage doc to backlog. :thumbsup:
